data.description: Backend Engineer with expertise in AWS, Java, and scalable system design

parameters.name: AWS Services Proficiency
parameters.description: DynamoDB, Lambda, S3 integration and hands-on implementation

depth_questions.question: I see you've started implementing AWS services. Can you explain your choice of DynamoDB for this use case and how it fits into your overall architecture?
depth_questions.correct_answer: DynamoDB is chosen for its serverless nature, automatic scaling, and seamless integration with Lambda. It provides consistent performance for the product catalog with flexible schema design.

depth_questions.question: How would you handle eventual consistency in your DynamoDB queries, especially for critical operations like inventory updates?
depth_questions.correct_answer: Use strongly consistent reads for critical operations, implement optimistic locking with version numbers, consider DynamoDB Streams for real-time updates, and design idempotent operations.

depth_questions.question: What would be your strategy for optimizing DynamoDB costs while maintaining performance at scale, and how would you monitor and troubleshoot performance issues?
depth_questions.correct_answer: Implement on-demand vs provisioned capacity analysis, use GSI efficiently, implement data archiving strategies, leverage DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for caching, monitor with CloudWatch metrics, and use X-Ray for distributed tracing.

parameters.name: Java & Spring Framework Expertise
milestones: Service layer and business logic completion
parameters.description: Backend development, REST APIs, microservices architecture

depth_questions.question: I notice you're using Spring Boot for your API. Can you walk me through your controller design and explain how you're handling request validation and response formatting?
depth_questions.correct_answer: Using @RestController with proper HTTP methods, implementing @Valid for request validation, using ResponseEntity for consistent response structure, and following REST conventions for endpoint design.

depth_questions.question: How are you managing transactions across multiple service calls, and what's your approach to handling distributed transactions in a microservices environment?
depth_questions.correct_answer: Using @Transactional for local transactions, implementing saga pattern for distributed transactions, considering eventual consistency, using compensating actions, and implementing circuit breaker patterns for resilience.

depth_questions.question: Explain your strategy for API versioning, backward compatibility, and how you would handle breaking changes in a production environment with multiple client applications?
depth_questions.correct_answer: Implement semantic versioning, use header-based or URL-based versioning, maintain backward compatibility through deprecation strategies, implement feature toggles, use API gateways for routing, and establish clear communication protocols for breaking changes.

parameters.name: System Integration & Data Management
parameters.description: API design, database operations, data migration concepts

depth_questions.question: I see you've designed your data model. Can you explain your approach to database schema design and how you're handling relationships between entities?
depth_questions.correct_answer: Using JPA entities with proper annotations, implementing appropriate relationships (OneToMany, ManyToOne), considering database normalization, using proper indexing strategies, and implementing soft deletes where needed.

depth_questions.question: How would you handle data migration from a legacy system while ensuring zero downtime and data consistency during the transition?
depth_questions.correct_answer: Implement blue-green deployment strategy, use database migration tools like Flyway, implement dual-write pattern during transition, perform data validation and reconciliation, use feature flags for gradual rollout, and maintain rollback capabilities.

depth_questions.question: Design a strategy for handling high-volume data processing, including batch processing, real-time streaming, and how you would ensure data quality and monitoring across the pipeline?
depth_questions.correct_answer: Implement event-driven architecture with Kafka/SQS, use batch processing with Spring Batch, implement data validation at multiple stages, use dead letter queues for error handling, implement comprehensive monitoring with metrics and alerting, and design for horizontal scaling.

masterProblem.title: Serverless Product Catalog API
masterProblem.description:
Build a Serverless Product Catalog System

You need to create a backend system for an e-commerce platform that manages product catalogs with the following requirements:

Core Requirements:

  • Product Management: Create, read, update, and delete products
  • Inventory Tracking: Real-time inventory updates with consistency
  • Search & Filtering: Support product search by category, price range, and availability
  • File Management: Handle product images and documents

Technical Specifications:

  • Use AWS Lambda for serverless compute
  • Use DynamoDB for product data storage
  • Use S3 for file storage
  • Implement Spring Boot with proper REST API design
  • Include proper error handling and validation
  • Consider scalability and performance optimization

Expected Implementation:

  1. Setup Phase: Configure AWS services and Spring Boot project structure
  2. API Development: Implement REST endpoints with proper validation
  3. Data Layer: Design database schema and implement data access patterns
  4. Integration: Connect all services with proper error handling

Focus Areas: Your solution will be evaluated on AWS service integration, Java/Spring implementation quality, and system design decisions.
